issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency: the problem statement uses the method name getFeedingSound() (e.g. 'getFeedingSound() should return "Arf Arf!"' for Seal and instructs feedAllAnimals() to call getFeedingSound()), but the template and solution define and use messageOnFeed() (Animal declares 'public abstract String messageOnFeed()', and Farm calls animal.messageOnFeed()). This mismatch can confuse students about which method to implement or call and may lead to incorrect implementations or test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. The simplest fix is to update problem_statement.md to replace all occurrences of getFeedingSound() with messageOnFeed(). Alternatively, keep the problem text and provide a getFeedingSound() wrapper in the code (e.g., add getFeedingSound() that delegates to messageOnFeed() in Animal or concrete classes) so both names work. Preferred: update the problem statement to reference messageOnFeed() to match the UML, template, and solution.

issues.description: The animal feeding-sound method is named inconsistently across the exercise materials. The UML and abstract Animal declaration in the problem statement reference messageOnFeed(), and the solution implementation uses public abstract String messageOnFeed() (Animal.java) and implements messageOnFeed() in the animal subclasses (Seal.java, Pig.java, Goat.java). However, several places in the problem statement's task descriptions refer to the same concept as getFeedingSound() (for Seal, Pig, and Goat). A student can be confused which method to implement or call: the problem text sometimes instructs getFeedingSound() while the implemented and required method (in the UML and solution) is messageOnFeed(), leading to possible wrong implementations, compilation errors or failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method identifier consistent across all artifacts. Replace all occurrences of getFeedingSound() in the problem statement with messageOnFeed(), so the UML, task descriptions, template hints, and solution consistently refer to messageOnFeed(). Alternatively, if renaming is preferred, rename the solution and template implementations to getFeedingSound() everywhere — but choose one identifier and apply it uniformly.
